raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's FFN activation fast path (`fused_silu_mul_bitexact`) is gated on `current_platform.is_cuda()`. On ROCm that predicate is `False` (`PlatformEnum.ROCM`), so the optimization is dead code on AMD hardware — even though the fused kernel is plain Triton (no CUDA JIT / PTX) and reproduces the eager `silu(a) * b` chain bit-exactly on HIP.

This is the same situation the XPU port fixed in #41940, which enabled the identical kernel via `(x.is_cuda or x.is_xpu)`. This PR does the equivalent for ROCm/HIP.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py`:

- Add `_silu_mul_device = current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_hip()`.

- Gate `QwenImage21FeedForward.forward` on `_silu_mul_device` instead of the vendor-pure `_is_cuda`.

Every other fast path in the module (RoPE, QK-norm, packed QKV, SDPA) stays CUDA-only, because those really are CUDA JIT / PTX kernels. The existing `BitExactFusionGate` still self-verifies the first call and permanently disables the path on any mismatch, so a platform that turns out not to be bit-exact falls back to eager instead of diverging.

`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_silu_mul_fusion.py` (new):

- assert the guard tracks the CUDA-like device family;

- assert `fused_silu_mul_bitexact` is bit-exact vs `F.silu(a) * b` at the FFN activation shapes.

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: AMD Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S Graphics, `gfx1151` (RDNA 3.5), torch `2.9.1+rocm7.2.4` (hip `7.2.53211`), SGLang Diffusion, attention backend `torch_sdpa`.

1. Kernel bit-exactness on `gfx1151` — `torch.equal(fused_silu_mul_bitexact(a, b), F.silu(a) * b)`:

   | shape           | max\_abs\_diff | bit-exact |
   | --------------- | -------------- | --------- |
   | (1, 4096, 3072) | 0.000e+00      | yes       |
   | (1, 2048, 3072) | 0.000e+00      | yes       |
   | (1, 1024, 3072) | 0.000e+00      | yes       |
   | (1, 4096, 2048) | 0.000e+00      | yes       |

2. End-to-end image output — Qwen-Image 2.1 @1024², 40 steps, seed 42. Two guard-OFF runs differ by *exactly* the same amount as guard-OFF vs guard-ON (max pixel diff 8; 173502 of 1048576 pixels differ). The residual difference is therefore entirely the pipeline's own run-to-run nondeterminism — the fusion adds no systematic deviation.

3. New unit test executed on ROCm with the platform probe working (the image ships the `amdsmi` bindings): `2 passed`; the bit-exact test covers the three FFN shapes via `subTest`. On ROCm images *without* `amdsmi` bindings, `multimodal_gen`'s probe falls back to CPU while `torch.cuda` still sees the GPU, so `test_guard_tracks_the_cuda_like_device_family` fails on its "unreachable on a CUDA-like device" assertion. That is a platform-detection gap tracked in #47296 (torch-based ROCm probe), not a property of this change; the RDNA4 report on #47296 shows both tests passing with it. The kernel-level bit-exactness test is unaffected either way.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per-call op timing (300 iters after warmup, `gfx1151`):

| shape           | eager    | fused    | speedup   |
| --------------- | -------- | -------- | --------- |
| (1, 4096, 3072) | 547.6 µs | 328.8 µs | **1.67x** |
| (1, 2048, 3072) | 167.5 µs | 130.1 µs | 1.29x     |
| (1, 1024, 3072) | 41.1 µs  | 25.6 µs  | 1.60x     |
| (1, 4096, 2048) | 354.5 µs | 219.9 µs | 1.61x     |

End-to-end — Qwen-Image 2.1 @1024², 40 steps, seed 42, `--dit-layerwise-offload --text-encoder-cpu-offload --pin-cpu-memory`, three runs per side:

| run                    | denoising stage (s)                | avg per-step (s)            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| guard OFF #1 / #2 / #3 | 156.86 / 157.46 / 159.77           | 3.2955 / 3.3066 / 3.3581    |
| guard ON  #1 / #2 / #3 | 159.00 / 154.66 / 155.50           | 3.3626 / 3.2684 / 3.2869    |
| **mean**               | **OFF 158.03 → ON 156.39 (−1.0%)** | **3.3201 → 3.3060 (−0.4%)** |

ON is faster in 2 of 3 pairs. The mean denoising delta (−1.0%) is within run-to-run noise at n=3 (per-run spread ≈1.5%), so the end-to-end figure should be read as *no regression, small favorable trend*. The deterministic part of the win is the kernel-level 1.67x; under `--dit-layerwise-offload` the FFN pointwise work partially overlaps weight prefetch, which masks most of it at this configuration.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(no doc change needed — no user-facing flag/behavior)*

- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Notes for reviewers

- `pre-commit run --files <two files>` passes every hook (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, check-chinese-characters, …).

- Reproduced on a ROCm-only machine; on a CUDA machine the guard evaluates to `True` exactly as before, so NVIDIA behavior is unchanged.

- Test-environment prerequisite: the guard test needs a working ROCm platform probe. Images whose `multimodal_gen` platform detection lacks the `amdsmi` Python bindings report CPU while `torch.cuda` still sees the GPU, so the guard test fails there regardless of this change. On gfx1151 the stock image (with `amdsmi`) gives `2 passed`; blocking `amdsmi` imports in a private overlay reproduces `1 failed, 1 passed` with the same assertion as the RDNA4 report. The fix is the torch-based ROCm probe tracked in #47296.

- Follow-ups (not in this PR): `ideogram.py:_ideogram_swiglu` uses the same kernel and is gated identically, and `rmsnorm_preserve_reduction` is pure Triton gated only on `torch.version.hip is None`.

@@ -65,6 +65,12 @@
 )
 
 _is_cuda = current_platform.is_cuda()
+# Every fast path below is a CUDA-only JIT or PTX kernel except the SiLU-mul
+# activation, which is plain Triton and rounds bit-exactly on HIP as well. That
+# one is gated on the device family instead of the vendor, so ROCm runs it too;
+# its BitExactFusionGate still verifies the first call and falls back on any
+# mismatch.
+_silu_mul_device = _is_cuda or current_platform.is_hip()
 
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 _ROPE_FUSION = BitExactFusionGate("Qwen-Image 2.1 complex RoPE")
@@ -436,7 +442,7 @@ def forward(self, x):
         gate, value = self.gate_layer(x)[0], self.proj(x)[0]
         fused = None
         if (
-            _is_cuda
+            _silu_mul_device
             and gate.dtype is torch.bfloat16
             and _SILU_MUL_FUSION.can_attempt_once()
         ):

@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Device guard and bit-exactness coverage for the Qwen-Image 2.1 SiLU-mul fusion.
+
+The fused activation is plain Triton, not a CUDA-only JIT/PTX kernel, so it is
+attempted on every CUDA-like device instead of NVIDIA hardware only. These tests
+pin the two facts that guard depends on: the guard itself tracks the device
+family, and the fused kernel still rounds bit-exactly against the eager
+``silu(a) * b`` chain it replaces.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import fused_silu_mul_bitexact
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.dits import qwen_image21 as model_module
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+class TestSiluMulFusionDeviceGuard(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_guard_tracks_the_cuda_like_device_family(self):
+        expected = current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_hip()
+        self.assertEqual(model_module._silu_mul_device, expected)
+        if torch.cuda.is_available():
+            self.assertTrue(
+                model_module._silu_mul_device,
+                "the fused SiLU-mul path is unreachable on a CUDA-like device",
+            )
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires a CUDA-like device")
+    def test_fused_silu_mul_is_bit_exact(self):
+        # The MLP widths Qwen-Image 2.1 actually feeds this kernel.
+        for shape in ((1, 2048, 3072), (1, 1024, 4096), (37, 1, 7)):
+            with self.subTest(shape=shape):
+                torch.manual_seed(0)
+                gate = torch.randn(*shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                value = torch.randn(*shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(
+                        fused_silu_mul_bitexact(gate, value), F.silu(gate) * value
+                    )
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

Thanks for testing this on RDNA4 (gfx1201) — the three-shape bit-exactness result matches what we see on gfx1151.

On the guard test: your diagnosis is correct, and it is not caused by this PR.

- `multimodal_gen`'s platform probe (`runtime/platforms/__init__.py::rocm_platform_plugin`) needs the `amdsmi` Python bindings. On images without them the plugin silently falls back to the CPU platform.
- `torch.cuda.is_available()` still returns `True` (torch has the HIP runtime), so in `test_guard_tracks_the_cuda_like_device_family` the `expected` value is `False` *and* the follow-up `assertTrue(model_module._silu_mul_device, "the fused SiLU-mul path is unreachable on a CUDA-like device")` fires. That is exactly the failure you saw.
- We did **not** apply #47296 on this box, so we cannot claim that fix as our own measurement; that result is yours. What we can confirm independently is the mechanism: on gfx1151 the stock image (which ships `amdsmi`) gives `2 passed`, while blocking `amdsmi` imports in a private overlay gives `1 failed, 1 passed` with the same `False is not true : the fused SiLU-mul path is unreachable on a CUDA-like device` assertion and the same test. That isolates the failure to the platform probe, not to this PR.
